name: 1 Apr 1955

references.label: Belfast Gazette issue 1746 (Alteration of boundary of Urban County District of Lisburn (confirmation of Antrim County Council order of 27 Jul 1954))
references.note: 10 Dec 1954, page 317. Made 3 Dec 1954. In force: 16 Feb 1955 (RPA); 1 Apr 1955 (all other purposes). Confirms the county council order (UDC proposal of 22 Oct 1952) extending Lisburn UD.

references.label: Census of Population 1961: General Report
references.note: Changes in administrative areas, Co. Antrim (i) (1 Apr 1955).

references.label: Urban Districts Boundaries (Procedure) Order (Northern Ireland) 1936 (S.R. & O. 1936 No. 170)
references.note: Made 9 Dec 1936 by the Ministry of Home Affairs under section 24 of the Local Government Act (Northern Ireland) 1934: the local inquiry and public notices required before a county council could make an order altering or defining the boundary of an urban county district. The Lisburn order confirmed 3 Dec 1954 recites compliance with it (Belfast Gazette, issue 1746, 10 Dec 1954).

references.label: Belfast Gazette issue 1746 (Lisburn Urban District (boundary alteration))
references.note: 10 Dec 1954, page 318. Made 27 Jul 1954. In force: 1 Apr 1955. District boundary altered: Urban District Boundary of Lisburn; places named: Lisburn Urban District, Moira, Clogher, County Antrim; by Ministry of Health and Local Government; made 27 July 1954; in force 1 April 1955; under Local Government Act (N.I.), 1934.

references.label: Belfast Gazette issue 1763 (Lisburn Urban District (boundary alteration))
references.note: 8 Apr 1955, page 114. In force: 1 Apr 1955. District boundary altered: REGISTRATION OF BIRTHS, DEATHS AND MARRIAGES REGISTRARS' DISTRICTS OF DUNMURRY, KNOCKNADONA AND LlSBURN; places named: Lisburn Urban District, Belfast, Clogher; in force 1 April 1955.

notes: 1 Apr 1955 reuses the converted geometry from 1 Apr 1950.

approximateSegments.note: Some lines on this map are approximate: parts of the Armagh urban district boundary are traced from the map deposited with the 1946 Order (about 20 m); parts of the Lurgan boundary are traced from the 1937 extension plan (about 25 m); parts of the Bangor borough boundary are traced from the 1950 extension plan (about 25 m). They are drawn dotted on the map.
